testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, look under the vehicle to:

options.text: Check if the vehicle is on an incline.
Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
Check if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting your vehicle, check its general condition. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or tree limbs.

questions.question: Before transporting an over-length load, what should you do?

options.text: Get special transit permits.
Alert fire departments along the route.
Pay tolls.

questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads require special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: During a winter pre-trip inspection, which item needs extra attention?

options.text: Coolant and antifreeze levels
The air conditioning unit
The oil pressure

questions.explanation: In winter, check your coolant level and antifreeze amount. Also check defrosting and heating equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer, tires and tire chains, lights and reflectors, windows and mirrors, handholds and steps, radiator shutters, and the exhaust system.

questions.question: When transporting livestock, drivers should be concerned about:

options.text: Other motorists seeing the livestock.
The vehicle's weight shifting as the animals move.
Extra tolls.
Passing emissions testing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's weight shifting as the animals move.
questions.explanation: Live animals can lean during curves and move while the vehicle is moving. This makes the weight distribution unstable. Driving with livestock requires extra care.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Not use mirrors because they are distracting.
Only use mirrors when there is traffic.
Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.explanation: You must know what is around you at all times. Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
Is one air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Has one system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the rear axle brakes, and the other controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: After two violations of state laws about hand-held mobile phone use:

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service.
Your CDL will be disqualified.
You must drive 10 mph under the speed limit for a period of time.

questions.explanation: If you are convicted twice of violating state laws about hand-held mobile phone use, your CDL will be disqualified. Punishments get worse with more violations.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Cannot be used on any vehicle.
Cannot be used on the front of a bus.
Cannot be used on trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be used on the front of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Ability to focus
Daydreaming
Yawning repeatedly
Drifting from your lane

questions.explanation: Fatigue while driving is dangerous. Warning signs include trouble focusing, repeated yawning or eye rubbing, daydreaming or wandering thoughts, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: Water on bridges:

options.text: Usually freezes before water on other parts of the roadway.
Usually freezes after water on other parts of the roadway.
Does not freeze.
Is not a concern in cool weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually freezes before water on other parts of the roadway.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the roadway. Be careful on bridges when temperatures are around freezing.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop a short distance later to:

options.text: Make sure the lug nuts are tight.
Lower the tire's air pressure.
Check if rocks are stuck in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later to check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should you check on your tires?

options.text: The air pressure.
The color.
The manufacturer.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that your tire pressure is correct — not too low and not too high.

questions.question: What can change how tall a vehicle sits?

options.text: Color
Length
Weight
Number of windows

questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower. A light load makes a vehicle sit higher. A vehicle that fits under an overpass when fully loaded may not fit when empty.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Before you start going down.
After you have already started going down.
As far down as possible.
At the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before starting down a hill. This helps you control your speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: When backing up a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around the truck first to check for obstacles.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the truck first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to look for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so do not rely only on them. Use a helper if possible.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park near trees and other vehicles.
Pull into a service station.
Park near other vehicles.
Park in an open, empty area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in an open, empty area.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area away from trees and other vehicles that could catch fire. Do not go to a service station.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Take a pep pill.
Stop and get some sleep.
Keep driving.

questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Pushing through fatigue is dangerous and can cause a deadly crash. Pep pills do not make you more alert.

questions.question: How do states make sure a CDL or CLP driver has only one license?

options.text: They call other states.
They use a computer system that connects all states.
They ask the driver.
They look through the driver's wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use a computer system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP license information in a shared database. When you apply for a license, the state checks this database to make sure you do not already have a license in another state.

questions.question: When it is hard to see your vehicle, such as at dawn or dusk, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your lights off.
Turn your lights on.
Drive on the shoulder.
Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When it is hard to see, turn your headlights on to low beam. If you are having trouble seeing others, they are probably having trouble seeing you.

questions.question: When are most drivers the least alert?

options.text: In the morning.
In cold weather.
At night.
After work.

questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Fatigue and lack of alertness are major dangers when driving at night.

questions.question: Air brakes are:

options.text: An effective way to stop large vehicles.
Not allowed on large vehicles.
Only work in bad weather.
A way to save fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: An effective way to stop large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Air brakes are safe and effective for stopping large, heavy vehicles when they are properly maintained.

questions.question: To work on a vehicle, ABS:

options.text: Must be on all axles.
Must be on the rear axle.
Can be on just one axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be on just one axle.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes on one axle give drivers better control when braking than having no anti-lock brakes at all.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Move your vehicle quickly.
Move your vehicle slowly.
Make a jerking motion with your vehicle.
You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly to stay in control of your vehicle. This also gives other drivers time to move out of your way. Always use your turn signal to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is encouraged:

options.text: Because the driver can see better.
Because turning toward the passenger side is illegal.
Because other drivers can help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because the driver can see better.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when possible. This gives you the best view of where your vehicle is going.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must provide:

options.text: Your fingerprints.
Your shoe size.
A list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.
Your work history for the last five years.

questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check.

questions.question: The air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.
How fast the vehicle goes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: When inspecting a vehicle, you must show all of the following except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge works.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off, or the gauge shows normal oil pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge, if the vehicle has one, rises to normal operating temperature.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: Check that the oil pressure gauge works and shows normal pressure, or that the warning light turns off. If your vehicle has an oil temperature gauge, it should rise to normal operating temperature. The oil pressure gauge should not come on when brakes are used.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
React to the driver's gestures.
Challenge the driver to a race.
Ignore the driver if possible.

questions.explanation: Get away from an aggressive driver if you can. Do not challenge them or make eye contact, and do not respond to rude gestures.

questions.question: When changing lanes, turn signals:

options.text: Should not be used.
Should only be used if a vehicle is close to you.
Should always be used.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you are signaling.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, you should:

options.text: Use hands-free cell phone devices.
Text instead of calling on your cell phone.
Not use your cell phone.
Turn up the ringer on your cell phone.

questions.explanation: Heavy traffic, road construction, pedestrians, and bad weather need your full attention. Avoid all distractions, including cell phone use.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a static leakage test in one minute?

options.text: 1 psi
2 psi
3 psi
4 psi

questions.explanation: The maximum air leakage for a single vehicle with air brakes is 2 psi in one minute. If the air brake system leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven because it needs repairs.

questions.question: What should you do if your engine catches fire?

options.text: Open the hood as soon as possible.
Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine immediately to stop an engine fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless necessary.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.
Press the accelerator.
Tap the accelerator twice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to set the parking brake and push it in to release it.

questions.question: In hot weather, where tar bleeds through the pavement:

options.text: The road is very slippery.
The road has the same traction as the rest of the pavement.
The road has more traction than the rest of the pavement.

questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. These spots are very slippery, so watch for them and be careful.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the air brakes.
Apply the parking brake.
Do not apply the brakes if the vehicle is out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle. You can also chock the wheels if needed.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: Check for leaks.
Make sure they are clear.
Make sure they are connected to the battery.
Make sure they have the right amount of play.

questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid levels, you should specifically check the hoses for any leaks.

questions.question: What happens to your vehicle's speed when traveling downhill?

options.text: It slows down.
It stays the same as on level roads.
It speeds up.

questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to speed up when going downhill. Reduce your speed before you reach a downgrade.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines during a vehicle inspection, which of the following should NOT be true?

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: Listen for leaks during your inspection. The air hoses and electrical lines should not be cut, chafed, spliced, or worn. They should not be tangled, pinched, or dragging against any parts.

questions.question: What condition should brake linings be in?

options.text: Loose.
Free of oil.
Soft.

questions.explanation: Brake linings should be free of oil and grease. They should not be loose or too thin.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is open space in the truck.
If the hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials can cause breathing problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of material is being carried and warn others about the hazards.

questions.question: What is true about pre-trip vehicle inspections?

options.text: They are not required if you use the vehicle regularly.
They are not required for trips under 100 miles.
Only a mechanic can perform them.
They are required by law.

questions.explanation: State and federal law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving.

questions.question: What should be true about the leaves in a leaf spring?

options.text: They may be broken.
They are not required.
They should not be broken.
They should shift.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle's suspension, check for broken or missing leaves in leaf springs. This is dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven.

questions.question: What happens when a driver is fatigued?

options.text: They become extra alert.
They should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake.
They may make important decisions too slowly.
They are usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: When fatigued, you will not see hazards or react to them as quickly. You will be slower at making important decisions.

questions.question: Why is backing a trailer toward the driver's side recommended?

options.text: The driver has the best view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver has the best view.
questions.explanation: When backing up, always back toward the left side of the vehicle. This gives the driver the best view of the rear.

questions.question: What should be checked during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: The engine oil level.
Removing coolant.
Spraying WD-40 into the air filter.
Removing a tire.

questions.explanation: A pre-trip inspection should include checks of engine compartment items, including the engine oil level.

questions.question: What do leaking shock absorbers mean?

options.text: They are normal.
They show a serious problem.
They will stop turn signals from working.
They are safe if the vehicle only drives on highways.

questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps a vehicle's axles in place. Damaged suspension parts like leaking shock absorbers are dangerous defects.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver?

options.text: Follow their vehicle closely.
Try to get their attention.
Stay far away from them.
Flash your lights at them.

questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space. Be careful when passing because they may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: How can you deal with blind spots?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only worry about vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
Avoid using your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to watch the traffic around you. This helps you notice if vehicles move into your blind spots.

questions.question: When starting a truck with a trailer, how can you tell the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right rear of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, dashboard lights should turn on and then off. If the ABS warning light stays on, the system is not working. On a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear stays on after starting, the ABS is not working properly.
